explanation: Potter first told the Peter Rabbit story in an illustrated letter to a sick child in 1893. Earnings from her books helped her buy Lake District farms, which she left to the National Trust.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The letter: The V&A's record describes it as an illustrated letter Potter sent to Noel Moore on 4 September 1893 while she was on holiday in Dunkeld. Why she wrote it: Noel was the five-year-old son of Potter's former governess, Annie Moore. He was recovering from scarlet fever, and Potter wrote the story to entertain him. The Tale of Peter Rabbit's Wikipedia entry gives the same account. The Morgan Library's record simply says he was recovering from an illness. Path to publication: In 1900 Annie Moore suggested the letters could become picture books. Potter borrowed the letter back and reworked it.

claimResults.note: The V&A (which holds the letter on loan) and the Morgan Library (Tier A), with Wikipedia: Potter's illustrated letter to Noel Moore, dated 4 September 1893 and written to entertain him while he was ill, first told Peter's story, and she later reworked it into the book. The sources differ only on the page count and on how they name the illness.
